question.text: Roshni Trust (education for disabled) holds a Section 12AB certificate that expires in 8 months from the date of NSE SSE application. The CFO insists that Section 12AB status exists and is 'sufficient'. As SIA, what is the CORRECT position under Table 3.1 of the SSE framework?

answer.text: The 12AB certificate must be valid for AT LEAST the next 12 months from the date of application.
Any valid 12AB certificate on the application date is sufficient; residual validity is immaterial.
The 12AB certificate must be valid for at least 24 months.
12AB is optional if the NPO has FCRA registration.

explanation.text: The Logic: Table 3.1 requires the Registration certificate under Section 12A/12AA/12AB/10(23C)/10(46) to be valid for at least the next 12 months from the date of application. An 8-month residual validity fails this test, and the SIA must flag it as a gating deficiency. The Trap: Option B ignores residual validity entirely. Option C doubles the threshold to 24 months. Option D wrongly equates FCRA with 12AB — they are separate regulatory regimes covering different streams. Note: Build a regulatory residual-validity matrix for every SSE engagement (date, expiry, months-to-expiry, renewal-in-progress) so any certificate under 12 months is identified as a hard stop early.
